summary: EEG predicts some healthy BOLD. Weak transfer and regional specificity shift the PhD focus to measurement, calibration and reliable abstention.
problem:
EEG: scalp electrical activity.
BOLD: blood oxygenation in fMRI.
One useful clinical decision?
takeaway: r measures aligned rises/falls; predictive R<super>2</super> also penalizes scale and offset errors. EEG ridge r .189, R<super>2</super> .028. Regional gain beyond a predicted-global template is uncertain (delta-r .004; 95% CI -.008 to .017).
methods: 27 people / 54 EC/EO runs. Three outer folds test unseen people; separate inner validation chooses settings. Compare 4/12 training people and 120/240 retained target-seconds; EEG power, sparse ECG timing or both. One subset order/MLP seed; four equal-weight MLP target groups. The 96 fitted cells reuse these people.
work_packages: Predict which montage/history/sensors add information; test rankings against cost-matched held-out choices.
Learn dynamics with missing EEG; test transfer beyond ridge, state templates and output recalibration.
Compare error at matched coverage. State assumptions: hidden vascular shifts can invalidate reliability.
clinical_gate:
Wakefulness advisory: compare direct EEG using independent events, false alerts/hour, delay and coverage.
Regional feedback: validate one patient ROI against paired fMRI, then test controlled benefit.
Clinical precedent: Prism's cleared adjunctive PTSD biofeedback excludes diagnostic interpretation [4].
Current limits: retrospective preprocessing, normalized targets, sparse ECG and one development site/seed. Live use and clinical benefit untested [5].
references:
[1] UnEBOLT, MIDL 2026. [2] UniEFS, ICML 2026.

[5] DECIDE-AI, 2022. Full sources: accompanying report.
